question: How do source-labelled WT RNA group-average log ratios differ between the first and second stimulation stages in the qualified GSE115504 reference table, and how sensitive is this point description to two fixed offsets?
decision: Complete the eligible RNA-only E6 description without inventing per-replicate values, uncertainty, genotype effects or a matched temporal RNA-ATAC panel.
strongest_rival: Averaged normalized values, source stage/control differences, low-expression offsets and absent replicate information can create a misleading impression of an individual history response or mechanistic persistence.
discriminator: Four exact WT source-average columns; separate within-stage log ratios, baseline shift and second-minus-first contrast; retain all rows and distinguish all-zero WT rows. Two prespecified offsets and independent full-table scalar arithmetic.
exposure_record: Original NAM N. brasiliensis-history/later-IAV context, published Daniel findings and E6 metadata/table headers are exposed. These source-average contrasts have not been computed. Same published source is one evidence lineage, not independent validation.
biological_unit: Published group-average RNA measurements, not individual samples; two title-labelled records per group do not recover per-replicate values or effective biological n.
nesting_and_overlap: The first/second-stage source columns are group averages. Across-stage animal/preparation overlap and averaging details are unqualified. Feature rows are not independent biological replicates.
population_and_selection: All 23420 source feature rows, exact four WT columns. KO columns are unused. All-zero WT rows remain in outputs and are counted separately; summaries of nonzero WT rows have an explicit denominator. No abundance threshold, chosen axis gene or outcome-dependent exclusion.
contrast: For offset c in {1,.5}: first=log2((WT_ctrl_3h_IL4+c)/(WT_ctrl_0h+c)); second=log2((WT_IL4_pre_3h_IL4+c)/(WT_IL4_pre_0h+c)); change=second-first; baseline=log2((WT_IL4_pre_0h+c)/(WT_ctrl_0h+c)). These describe source group averages, not means of individual log responses or a causal interaction.
endpoint: Unranked row-level source-average contrasts; same/opposite/zero direction counts and descriptive across-row quantiles, by fixed offset. No variance, confidence intervals, p-values or effective n.
methods: Read only the four qualified WT columns; no re-normalization of source-labelled averaged CPM. Compute numpy log differences and independently verify every value with Python math.log2 ratios/product ratios at absolute tolerance 1e-11. Retain all source rows; separate all-zero WT rows from the nonzero-row denominator. Plot unlabelled feature-density geometry, no selected loci.
missingness_and_exclusions: Invalid nonfinite/negative averages or changed source headers stop. No genotype contrast, no recovered individual values, no ambiguous time-course interpolation, and no exclusion to align results with a regulatory axis.
multiplicity: No hypothesis tests or population claims. Across-row proportions and quantiles describe this table; they are not independent biological replication or uncertainty.
precision_basis: Replicate-level measurements are absent from the group-average table. Biological variance and precision remain unknown; numerical tolerance verifies floating-point arithmetic only.
interpretation_limit: The table is author-labelled averaged CPM with unverified normalization details. Point ratios can describe those averages, but not individual temporal responses, biological uncertainty, post-cessation NAM memory, activity, binding, enzyme output or mechanistic causation. No matching to unrelated ATAC or muscle samples.
stop_rule: Stop and preserve failure on source/hash/column/number/arithmetic conflicts. Keep both offset outcomes and all mixed/zero directions; do not add targets, genotypes or thresholds to obtain an appealing pattern.
amendment_reason: Owner-authorized RNA-only E6 point description after exact source qualification; all temporal/cross-assay and biological inference limits remain explicit.
